stem: The diagram shows a net of a cuboid with edges $8$ cm, $5$ cm and $4$ cm. An ant crawls on the surface from corner $A$ to opposite corner $G$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly identifies a shortest surface path?

options.text: On the net that joins faces into a $5$-by-$12$ rectangle, the straight $A$-to-$G$ segment has length $13$ cm, shortest among the three standard unfolds.
The shortest surface path is $\sqrt{8^{2}+5^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{105}$ cm, the interior space diagonal.
Adding $8+5+4=17$ cm gives the shortest surface path.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that compares unfold lengths.

part_answers.answer: The three standard unfolds give $\sqrt{8^{2}+9^{2}}=\sqrt{145}$, $\sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}=13$, and $\sqrt{4^{2}+13^{2}}=\sqrt{185}$; the least is $13$ cm on the $5$-by-$12$ net. The space diagonal and edge sum are not surface paths.

teacher.key_rationale: Unfold lengths √145, 13, √185; shortest is 13 on the 5-by-12 net. Space diagonal and edge sum are not surface paths.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as cuboid net 8×5×4 with dashed A-to-G path on the 5-by-12 unfold.
